Counted from the upstream files only, never through ERD Studio: SQL by a replaying statement reader (comments, strings, $$ bodies, DELIMITER and GO handled; CREATE/ALTER/DROP TABLE, ADD/DROP/RENAME/ALTER COLUMN, ADD/DROP CONSTRAINT incl. PostgreSQL default constraint names, RENAME TO, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, COMMENT ON, MS_Description, USE SCHEMA, ALTER TABLE inside DO blocks), DBML/TMDL by line readers, model.bim as JSON, dbt by parsing models/**/*.yml.

Every count was checked against the independently counted numbers in each sample's SOURCE.md (the "counts" object). Columns are [name, type, flags, description?] with flags P primary key, N not null, U unique, C calculated.
Relationships are one entry per column pair from the FK (many) side; a composite FK shares "composite". "notes" says where a sample's truth needs a reading.

SQL samples are checked against the real engines (test/real-world-truth/, docs/dev/real-world-truth.md): every difference between this file and the engines' catalogs is explained in test/real-world-truth/differences.json.

postgres-pagila.notes: payment is partitioned (PARTITION BY RANGE): its 55 monthly partitions are CREATE TABLE ... (the same 7 columns) joined by ALTER TABLE ONLY payment ATTACH PARTITION. They have no columns of their own, so the logical model folds them into payment (SOURCE.md, "If an importer folds the partitions"): 16 tables, 94 columns, 16 primary keys, 22 relationships, the 18 partition FKs being 3 distinct ones from payment to customer, rental and staff (the parent declares none). Kept as tables (the import's 'Keep each partition as a table') they are 71 tables, 479 columns and 37 FKs. length_hours is a PostgreSQL 18 VIRTUAL generated column.

postgres-pagila-partitions-kept.notes: The same pg_dump as postgres-pagila, imported with 'Keep each partition as a table' (input.partitions 'tables'): payment's 55 monthly partitions are CREATE TABLE ... (the same 7 columns) of their own and count as tables, as SOURCE.md counts them (71 tables, 479 columns, 37 FKs: the 18 FKs pg_dump declares only on partitions 2022_01..06 included). Each partition also has payment's primary key (payment_date, payment_id) and unique index (uuid, payment_date): the dump writes neither on a partition, but PostgreSQL creates both when a partition is attached (read back from PostgreSQL 18, test/real-world-truth/engine/postgres-pagila.json), so 71 primary keys, not SOURCE.md's 16. This is the truth the scorecard held before folding became the default, kept so the kept-as-tables reading of a real dump stays measured. length_hours is a PostgreSQL 18 VIRTUAL generated column.

mysql-sakila.notes: address.location is declared inside MySQL versioned comments (/*!50705 ... */), which MySQL executes, so it is a column. The CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE inside rewards_report is not a table.

sqlserver-adventureworks.notes: Types are as written ([nvarchar](60), alias types such as [dbo].[Name]); computed columns have no type ("(computed)"). Descriptions are MS_Description extended properties. 2 unique indexes on views are not table keys. A computed column of ISNULL(expr, constant) is NOT NULL (SQL Server 2025 sys.columns.is_nullable = 0, test/real-world-truth/engine/sqlserver-adventureworks.json): Customer.AccountNumber, PurchaseOrderDetail.LineTotal, PurchaseOrderDetail.StockedQty, SalesOrderDetail.LineTotal, SalesOrderHeader.SalesOrderNumber, SalesOrderHeader.TotalDue, WorkOrder.StockedQty.

tables.name: consent
tables.description: ORDM canonical-core customer consent — the single source of truth for opt-ins and processing permissions.
columns: Surrogate key. Unique per consent version.
Durable natural/business key for the consent record.
Durable business key of the customer giving/withholding consent.

What the consent governs. third_party_sharing = disclosure of personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising (CCPA/CPRA do-not-SHARE); data_sale = disclosure for monetary or other valuable consideration (CCPA/CPRA do-not-SELL) - the two are legally distinct opt-outs (the mandated link reads Do Not Sell or Share), so they are separate types, not one. Allowed values: marketing_email, marketing_sms, marketing_phone, marketing_postal, data_processing, third_party_sharing, data_sale, profiling, cookies.
Current decision. Allowed values: granted, withdrawn, pending, expired.
Lawful basis for processing. Allowed values: consent, contract, legitimate_interest, legal_obligation, vital_interest, public_task.
Channel where consent was captured (vendor-neutral). Allowed values: web, mobile_app, store, call_center, email.
Identifier/version of the consent statement or privacy notice presented at capture.

Region/law scope this decision applies under. May be an ISO 3166-1 country (GB), an ISO 3166-2 subdivision (US-CA), or a reserved regional code (EU) — not alpha-2-only, since regulatory scope does not map cleanly to countries. Lets one customer hold different consent per jurisdiction (GDPR vs CCPA/CPRA). NULL = global/unspecified.

Operational do-not-activate overlay for this consent scope. TRUE = suppress activation on this purpose x channel even when consent_status is granted (suppression OVERRIDES consent). Distinct from withdrawal (consent_status=withdrawn is the customer revoking permission; suppression is an operational/legal do-not-contact signal, e.g. hard bounce or a direct-marketing objection). NULL/FALSE = not suppressed.

Why this scope is suppressed (set only when suppression_indicator is TRUE). Two scopes: CHANNEL-level reasons block only this consent scope (unsubscribe, hard_bounce, spam_complaint, list_hygiene); PERSON-level reasons block every plane for the profile (deceased, fraud, do_not_contact, legal_objection) via the shared UCV gold_person_do_not_target_current view, which both the owned activation gate and any paid/non-owned plane consult (ADR 0028). Allowed values: unsubscribe, hard_bounce, spam_complaint, legal_objection, deceased, fraud, do_not_contact, list_hygiene.
SCD2: inclusive start date this consent version became effective.
SCD2: exclusive end date; NULL while still in effect.
SCD2: TRUE for the currently effective consent record per (profile, consent_type, jurisdiction_code).
Legal-grade instant the consent decision was given/withdrawn (UTC, ISO 8601).

tables.name: touchpoint
tables.description: ORDM canonical-core conformed omnichannel customer-interaction fact (append-only). The time-series touch class of the two-class CDP shape, online + offline, kept separate from the customer profile.
columns: Surrogate key. Unique per interaction row.
Durable natural/business key for the interaction, unique at row grain.
Hashed/tokenized device/cookie/app identifier — the anonymous digital actor key. Never a raw device id, cookie, or IP (PII, pseudonymized). NULL for offline touches (identity-first).
Session/visit grouping key for sessionization (degenerate attribute; vendor-neutral, no PII). NULL for touches with no session (e.g. a single call-center contact).
FK to customer.identity_link.identity_link_sk — the assertion that stitched this device/actor to a profile, if resolved.
FK to customer.profile.profile_sk (resolved as-of event_date), if the touch is stitched to a known customer.

Durable customer business key (pseudonymous; NULL while the touch is anonymous). Resolved AT INGEST: this fact is append-only, so a touch that was anonymous when written stays profile_id=NULL even after the device is later stitched - late resolution is re-derived at query time by joining device_id_hash through customer.identity_link (touchpoint_resolved_rate is therefore an at-ingest rate, not lifetime).

The kind of touch. Digital: page_view, product_view, search, add_to_cart, remove_from_cart, cart_view, checkout_start, wishlist_add, app_open, session_start, session_end. Offline: store_visit, call_center_contact, kiosk_session, offline_marketing_response, phone_activation.
Channel the touch occurred on (omnichannel discriminator). The coarse MEDIUM. Allowed values: web, mobile_app, in_store, kiosk, call_center, direct_mail, other.

The specific application / property / data stream the touch came from (degenerate attribute; vendor-neutral, no PII). The SOURCE that pairs with channel_code (the medium), mirroring how a CDP pairs channel with source/data-stream on each event. Allowed values: ios_app, android_app, web_desktop, web_mobile, loyalty_kiosk, in_store_pos, call_center_app, email_platform, other.
Whether the touch is customer-initiated or brand-initiated. Allowed values: inbound, outbound.
When the touch occurred at source (UTC, ISO 8601).

Business date of the touch (cluster key). This IS the date_key-role natural key (the same calendar-join role sales.date_key plays), joined to fiscal_calendar.date_key (ISO 8601); it is named event_date for event semantics (ADR 0011 permits role-named stems). Guarded by the touchpoint_calendar_coverage DQ check. No surrogate FK, matching the sales convention.
When this touch was ingested into the lakehouse (UTC, ISO 8601).
Seconds between event_timestamp and ingest_timestamp (freshness monitoring).
FK to product.product_sk (version as-of event_date) — set for product_view / cart touches.
FK to store.store_sk — in-store / kiosk / store-visit context, or the fulfilling store.
Page/screen class for digital touches. Allowed values: home, category, product, search, cart, checkout, account, content, other.
De-identified/normalized page path (source contract: no PII, no PII-bearing query params). NULL for offline touches.
De-identified/normalized referrer path (source contract: no PII).
Shopper search query for search touches (degenerate attribute; vendor-neutral; source contract: de-identified, no PII - a shopper may type a name/email, so ingest must scrub).

Engagement depth: seconds spent on the touch, if known. CROSS-MODAL by interaction_type - page dwell (digital), call duration (call_center), or visit length (store_visit) - so these are NOT the same unit of comparability. A consumer averaging dwell across interaction_type blends incomparable durations; restrict to one modality (e.g. digital page_view/product_view) for a comparable engagement metric. NULL if not captured.
Cart correlation key linking cart touches within a shopping journey (degenerate; no FK).
Order correlation key when a checkout touch converts (degenerate business key to the order; no surrogate FK, header-grain).
Monetary value the touch carries, if any (e.g. cart value), in the reporting/base currency.
Reporting/base currency of event_value_amount, ISO 4217 alpha-3 (single-currency by construction).
Consent state at touch time. Allowed values: granted, denied, unknown.

tables.name: concept
tables.description: The Standardized Vocabularies contains records, or Concepts, that uniquely identify each fundamental unit of meaning used to express clinical information in all domain tables of the CDM. Concepts are derived from vocabularies, which represent clinical information across a domain (e.g. conditions, drugs, procedures) through the use of codes and associated descriptions. Some Concepts are designated Standard Concepts, meaning these Concepts can be used as normative expressions of a clinical entity within the OMOP Common Data Model and standardized analytics. Each Standard Concept belongs to one Domain, which defines the location where the Concept would be expected to occur within the data tables of the CDM. Concepts can represent broad categories ('Cardiovascular disease'), detailed clinical elements ('Myocardial infarction of the anterolateral wall'), or modifying characteristics and attributes that define Concepts at various levels of detail (severity of a disease, associated morphology, etc.). Records in the Standardized Vocabularies tables are derived from national or international vocabularies such as SNOMED-CT, RxNorm, and LOINC, or custom OMOP Concepts defined to cover various aspects of observational data analysis.
columns: A unique identifier for each Concept across all domains.
An unambiguous, meaningful and descriptive name for the Concept.
A foreign key to the [DOMAIN](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html#domain) table the Concept belongs to.
A foreign key to the [VOCABULARY](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html#vocabulary) table indicating from which source the Concept has been adapted.
The attribute or concept class of the Concept. Examples are 'Clinical Drug', 'Ingredient', 'Clinical Finding' etc.

This flag determines where a Concept is a Standard Concept, i.e. is used in the data, a Classification Concept, or a non-standard Source Concept. The allowable values are 'S' (Standard Concept) and 'C' (Classification Concept), otherwise the content is NULL.
The concept code represents the identifier of the Concept in the source vocabulary, such as SNOMED-CT concept IDs, RxNorm RXCUIs etc. Note that concept codes are not unique across vocabularies.
The date when the Concept was first recorded. The default value is 1-Jan-1970, meaning, the Concept has no (known) date of inception.
The date when the Concept became invalid because it was deleted or superseded (updated) by a new concept. The default value is 31-Dec-2099, meaning, the Concept is valid until it becomes deprecated.
Reason the Concept was invalidated. Possible values are D (deleted), U (replaced with an update) or NULL when valid_end_date has the default value.

tables.name: concept_ancestor
tables.description: The CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table is designed to simplify observational analysis by providing the complete hierarchical relationships between Concepts. Only direct parent-child relationships between Concepts are stored in the CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP table. To determine higher-level ancestry connections, all individual direct relationships would have to be navigated at analysis time. The CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table includes records for all parent-child relationships, as well as grandparent-grandchild relationships and those of any other level of lineage for Standard or Classification concepts. Using the CONCEPT_ANCESTOR table allows for querying for all descendants of a hierarchical concept, and the other way around. For example, drug ingredients and drug products, beneath them in the hierarchy, are all descendants of a drug class ancestor. This table is entirely derived from the CONCEPT, CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP, and RELATIONSHIP tables.
columns: The Concept Id for the higher-level concept that forms the ancestor in the relationship.
The Concept Id for the lower-level concept that forms the descendant in the relationship.
The minimum separation in number of levels of hierarchy between ancestor and descendant concepts. This is an attribute that is used to simplify hierarchic analysis.
The maximum separation in number of levels of hierarchy between ancestor and descendant concepts. This is an attribute that is used to simplify hierarchic analysis.

Concept Classes represent so-called horizontal (e.g. MedDRA, RxNorm) or vertical levels (e.g. SNOMED) of the vocabulary structure. Vocabularies without any Concept Classes, such as HCPCS, use the vocabulary_id as the Concept Class. This reference table is populated with a single record for each Concept Class, which includes a Concept Class ID and a fully specified Concept Class name.
columns: A unique key for each class.

A Concept that represents the Concept Class.

This table captures various types of relationships, including hierarchical, associative, and other semantic connections, enabling comprehensive analysis and interpretation of clinical concepts. Every kind of relationship is defined in the RELATIONSHIP table.

tables.name: condition_era
tables.description: A Condition Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to have a given condition. Similar to Drug Eras, Condition Eras are chronological periods of Condition Occurrence and every Condition Occurrence record should be part of a Condition Era. Combining individual Condition Occurrences into a single Condition Era serves two purposes:  - It allows aggregation of chronic conditions that require frequent ongoing care, instead of treating each Condition Occurrence as an independent event. - It allows aggregation of multiple, closely timed doctor visits for the same Condition to avoid double-counting the Condition Occurrences. For example, consider a Person who visits her Primary Care Physician (PCP) and who is referred to a specialist. At a later time, the Person visits the specialist, who confirms the PCP's original diagnosis and provides the appropriate treatment to resolve the condition. These two independent doctor visits should be aggregated into one Condition Era.
columns: The Concept Id representing the Condition.

The start date for the Condition Era constructed from the individual instances of Condition Occurrences. It is the start date of the very first chronologically recorded instance of the condition with at least 31 days since any prior record of the same Condition.
The end date for the Condition Era constructed from the individual instances of Condition Occurrences. It is the end date of the final continuously recorded instance of the Condition.
The number of individual Condition Occurrences used to construct the condition era.

tables.name: dose_era
tables.description: A Dose Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to be exposed to a constant dose of a specific active ingredient.
columns: The Concept Id representing the specific drug ingredient.
The Concept Id representing the unit of the specific drug ingredient.
The numeric value of the dosage of the drug_ingredient.
The date the Person started on the specific dosage, with at least 31 days since any prior exposure.

tables.name: drug_era
tables.description: A Drug Era is defined as a span of time when the Person is assumed to be exposed to a particular active ingredient. A Drug Era is not the same as a Drug Exposure: Exposures are individual records corresponding to the source when Drug was delivered to the Person, while successive periods of Drug Exposures are combined under certain rules to produce continuous Drug Eras. Every record in the DRUG_EXPOSURE table should be part of a drug era based on the dates of exposure.
columns: The drug_concept_id should conform to the concept class 'ingredient' as the drug_era is an era of time where a person is exposed to a particular drug ingredient.
The count of grouped DRUG_EXPOSURE records that were included in the DRUG_ERA row

tables.name: drug_exposure
tables.description: This table captures records about the exposure to a Drug ingested or otherwise introduced into the body. A Drug is a biochemical substance formulated in such a way that when administered to a Person it will exert a certain biochemical effect on the metabolism. Drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vaccines, and large-molecule biologic therapies. Radiological devices ingested or applied locally do not count as Drugs.
columns: The unique key given to records of drug dispensings or administrations for a person. Refer to the ETL for how duplicate drugs during the same visit were handled.
The PERSON_ID of the PERSON for whom the drug dispensing or administration is recorded. This may be a system generated code.

The DRUG_CONCEPT_ID field is recommended for primary use in analyses, and must be used for network studies. This is the standard concept mapped from the source concept id which represents a drug product or molecule otherwise introduced to the body. The drug concepts can have a varying degree of information about drug strength and dose. This information is relevant in the context of quantity and administration information in the subsequent fields plus strength information from the DRUG_STRENGTH table, provided as part of the standard vocabulary download.
Use this date to determine the start date of the drug record.
The DRUG_EXPOSURE_END_DATE denotes the day the drug exposure ended for the patient.
This is the end date of the drug exposure as it appears in the source data, if it is given
You can use the TYPE_CONCEPT_ID to delineate between prescriptions written vs. prescriptions dispensed vs. medication history vs. patient-reported exposure, etc.
The reason a person stopped a medication as it is represented in the source. Reasons include regimen completed, changed, removed, etc. This field will be retired in v6.0.
This is only filled in when the record is coming from a prescription written this field is meant to represent intended refills at time of the prescription.
This is the verbatim instruction for the drug as written by the provider.
The Provider associated with drug record, e.g. the provider who wrote the prescription or the provider who administered the drug.
The Visit during which the drug was prescribed, administered or dispensed.

The VISIT_DETAIL record during which the drug exposure occurred. For example, if the person was in the ICU at the time of the drug administration the VISIT_OCCURRENCE record would reflect the overall hospital stay and the VISIT_DETAIL record would reflect the ICU stay during the hospital visit.
This field houses the verbatim value from the source data representing the drug exposure that occurred. For example, this could be an NDC or Gemscript code.

This is the concept representing the drug source value and may not necessarily be standard. This field is discouraged from use in analysis because it is not required to contain Standard Concepts that are used across the OHDSI community, and should only be used when Standard Concepts do not adequately represent the source detail for the Drug necessary for a given analytic use case. Consider using DRUG_CONCEPT_ID instead to enable standardized analytics that can be consistent across the network.
This field houses the verbatim value from the source data representing the drug route.
This field houses the verbatim value from the source data representing the dose unit of the drug given.

tables.name: drug_strength
tables.description: The DRUG_STRENGTH table contains structured content about the amount or concentration and associated units of a specific ingredient contained within a particular drug product. This table is supplemental information to support standardized analysis of drug utilization.
columns: The Concept representing the Branded Drug or Clinical Drug Product.
The Concept representing the active ingredient contained within the drug product.
The numeric value or the amount of active ingredient contained within the drug product.
The Concept representing the Unit of measure for the amount of active ingredient contained within the drug product.
The concentration of the active ingredient contained within the drug product.
The Concept representing the Unit of measure for the concentration of active ingredient.
The amount of total liquid (or other divisible product, such as ointment, gel, spray, etc.).
The Concept representing the denominator unit for the concentration of active ingredient.
The number of units of Clinical Branded Drug or Quantified Clinical or Branded Drug contained in a box as dispensed to the patient.
The date when the Concept was first recorded. The default value is 1-Jan-1970.
The date when then Concept became invalid.
Reason the concept was invalidated. Possible values are D (deleted), U (replaced with an update) or NULL when valid_end_date has the default value.

tables.name: episode
tables.description: The EPISODE table aggregates lower-level clinical events (VISIT_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, DEVICE_EXPOSURE) into a higher-level abstraction representing clinically and analytically relevant disease phases,outcomes and treatments. The EPISODE_EVENT table connects qualifying clinical events (VISIT_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, DEVICE_EXPOSURE) to the appropriate EPISODE entry. For example cancers including their development over time, their treatment, and final resolution.
columns: A unique identifier for each Episode.
The PERSON_ID of the PERSON for whom the episode is recorded.
The EPISODE_CONCEPT_ID represents the kind abstraction related to the disease phase, outcome or treatment.
The date when the Episode beings.
The date and time when the Episode begins.
The date when the instance of the Episode is considered to have ended.
The date when the instance of the Episode is considered to have ended.
Use this field to find the Episode that subsumes the given Episode record. This is used in the case that an Episode are nested into each other.
For sequences of episodes, this is used to indicate the order the episodes occurred. For example, lines of treatment could be indicated here.

A Standard Concept representing the disease phase, outcome, or other abstraction of which the episode consists.  For example, if the EPISODE_CONCEPT_ID is [treatment regimen](https://athena.ohdsi.org/search-terms/terms/32531) then the EPISODE_OBJECT_CONCEPT_ID should contain the chemotherapy regimen concept, like [Afatinib monotherapy](https://athena.ohdsi.org/search-terms/terms/35804392).
This field can be used to determine the provenance of the Episode record, as in whether the episode was from an EHR system, insurance claim, registry, or other sources.

The source code for the Episode as it appears in the source data. This code is mapped to a Standard Condition Concept in the Standardized Vocabularies and the original code is stored here for reference.
A foreign key to a Episode Concept that refers to the code used in the source.

tables.name: episode_event
tables.description: The EPISODE_EVENT table connects qualifying clinical events (such as CONDITION_OCCURRENCE, DRUG_EXPOSURE, PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE, MEASUREMENT) to the appropriate EPISODE entry. For example, linking the precise location of the metastasis (cancer modifier in MEASUREMENT) to the disease episode.
columns: Use this field to link the EPISODE_EVENT record to its EPISODE.

This field is the primary key of the linked record in the database. For example, if the Episode Event is a Condition Occurrence, then the CONDITION_OCCURRENCE_ID of the linked record goes in this field.
This field is the CONCEPT_ID that identifies which table the primary key of the linked record came from.

tables.name: fact_relationship
tables.description: The FACT_RELATIONSHIP table contains records about the relationships between facts stored as records in any table of the CDM. Relationships can be defined between facts from the same domain, or different domains. Examples of Fact Relationships include: [Person relationships](https://athena.ohdsi.org/search-terms/terms?domain=Relationship&standardConcept=Standard&page=2&pageSize=15&query=) (parent-child), care site relationships (hierarchical organizational structure of facilities within a health system), indication relationship (between drug exposures and associated conditions), usage relationships (of devices during the course of an associated procedure), or facts derived from one another (measurements derived from an associated specimen).

tables.name: location
tables.description: The LOCATION table represents a generic way to capture physical location or address information of Persons and Care Sites.
columns: The unique key given to a unique Location.
This is the first line of the address.
This is the second line of the address

The Concept Id representing the country. Values should conform to the [Geography](https://athena.ohdsi.org/search-terms/terms?domain=Geography&standardConcept=Standard&page=1&pageSize=15&query=&boosts) domain.

tables.name: measurement
tables.description: The MEASUREMENT table contains records of Measurements, i.e. structured values (numerical or categorical) obtained through systematic and standardized examination or testing of a Person or Person's sample. The MEASUREMENT table contains both orders and results of such Measurements as laboratory tests, vital signs, quantitative findings from pathology reports, etc. Measurements are stored as attribute value pairs, with the attribute as the Measurement Concept and the value representing the result. The value can be a Concept (stored in VALUE_AS_CONCEPT), or a numerical value (VALUE_AS_NUMBER) with a Unit (UNIT_CONCEPT_ID). The Procedure for obtaining the sample is housed in the PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE table, though it is unnecessary to create a PROCEDURE_OCCURRENCE record for each measurement if one does not exist in the source data. Measurements differ from Observations in that they require a standardized test or some other activity to generate a quantitative or qualitative result. If there is no result, it is assumed that the lab test was conducted but the result was not captured.
columns: The unique key given to a Measurement record for a Person. Refer to the ETL for how duplicate Measurements during the same Visit were handled.
The PERSON_ID of the Person for whom the Measurement is recorded. This may be a system generated code.

The MEASUREMENT_CONCEPT_ID field is recommended for primary use in analyses, and must be used for network studies. This is the standard concept mapped from the source value which represents a measurement.
Use this date to determine the date of the measurement.
This field can be used to determine the provenance of the Measurement record, as in whether the measurement was from an EHR system, insurance claim, registry, or other sources.

The meaning of Concept [4172703](https://athena.ohdsi.org/search-terms/terms/4172703) for '=' is identical to omission of a OPERATOR_CONCEPT_ID value. Since the use of this field is rare, it's important when devising analyses to not to forget testing for the content of this field for values different from =.

This is the numerical value of the Result of the Measurement, if available. Note that measurements such as blood pressures will be split into their component parts i.e. one record for systolic, one record for diastolic.
If the raw data gives a categorial result for measurements those values are captured and mapped to standard concepts in the 'Meas Value' domain.

At present, there isn't a prescribed unit for individual measurements, such as Hemoglobin A1C, meaning it's not obligatory to express these measurements as a percentage. UNIT_SOURCE_VALUES should be linked to a Standard Concept within the Unit domain that most accurately reflects the unit provided in the source data.
Ranges have the same unit as the VALUE_AS_NUMBER. These ranges are provided by the source and should remain NULL if not given.
Ranges have the same unit as the VALUE_AS_NUMBER. These ranges are provided by the source and should remain NULL if not given.
The provider associated with measurement record, e.g. the provider who ordered the test or the provider who recorded the result.
The visit during which the Measurement occurred.

The VISIT_DETAIL record during which the Measurement occurred. For example, if the Person was in the ICU at the time the VISIT_OCCURRENCE record would reflect the overall hospital stay and the VISIT_DETAIL record would reflect the ICU stay during the hospital visit.
This field contains the exact value from the source data that represents the measurement that occurred.

This is the concept representing the MEASUREMENT_SOURCE_VALUE and may not necessarily be standard. This field is discouraged from use in analysis because it is not required to contain Standard Concepts that are used across the OHDSI community, and should only be used when Standard Concepts do not adequately represent the source detail for the Measurement necessary for a given analytic use case. Consider using MEASUREMENT_CONCEPT_ID instead to enable standardized analytics that can be consistent across the network.
This field contains the exact value from the source data that represents the unit of measurement used.

"This is the concept representing the UNIT_SOURCE_VALUE and may not necessarily be standard. This field is discouraged from use in analysis because it is not required to contain Standard Concepts that are used across the OHDSI community, and should only be used when Standard Concepts do not adequately represent the source detail for the Measurement necessary for a given analytic use case. Consider using UNIT_CONCEPT_ID instead to enable standardized analytics that can be consistent across the network."
This field houses the verbatim result value of the Measurement from the source data .
If the Measurement record is related to another record in the database, this field is the primary key of the linked record.
If the Measurement record is related to another record in the database, this field is the CONCEPT_ID that identifies which table the primary key of the linked record came from.

tables.name: metadata
tables.description: The METADATA table contains metadata information about a dataset that has been transformed to the OMOP Common Data Model.
columns: The unique key given to a Metadata record.

This is the numerical value of the result of the Metadata, if applicable and available. It is not expected that all Metadata will have numeric results, rather, this field is here to house values should they exist.

tables.name: note
tables.description: The NOTE table captures unstructured information that was recorded by a provider about a patient in free text (in ASCII, or preferably in UTF8 format) notes on a given date. The type of note_text is CLOB or varchar(MAX) depending on RDBMS.
columns: A unique identifier for each note.
The date the note was recorded.
The provenance of the note. Most likely this will be EHR.
A Standard Concept Id representing the HL7 LOINC Document Type Vocabulary classification of the note.
This is the Concept representing the character encoding type.
The Provider who wrote the note.
The Visit during which the note was written.
The Visit Detail during which the note was written.
If the Note record is related to another record in the database, this field is the primary key of the linked record.
If the Note record is related to another record in the database, this field is the CONCEPT_ID that identifies which table the primary key of the linked record came from.

tables.name: note_nlp
tables.description: The NOTE_NLP table encodes all output of NLP on clinical notes. Each row represents a single extracted term from a note.
columns: A unique identifier for the NLP record.
This is the NOTE_ID for the NOTE record the NLP record is associated to.
A small window of text surrounding the term
Character offset of the extracted term in the input note
Raw text extracted from the NLP tool.
The date of the note processing.
The date and time of the note processing.

tables.name: observation
tables.description: The OBSERVATION table captures clinical facts about a Person obtained in the context of examination, questioning or a procedure. Any data that cannot be represented by any other domains, such as social and lifestyle facts, medical history, family history, etc. are recorded here.
columns: The unique key given to an Observation record for a Person. Refer to the ETL for how duplicate Observations during the same Visit were handled.
The PERSON_ID of the Person for whom the Observation is recorded. This may be a system generated code.
The OBSERVATION_CONCEPT_ID field is recommended for primary use in analyses, and must be used for network studies.

The date of when the Observation was obtained. Depending on what the Observation represents this could be the date of a lab test, the date of a survey, or the date a patient's family history was taken.
This field can be used to determine the provenance of the Observation record, as in whether the measurement was from an EHR system, insurance claim, registry, or other sources.

This is the numerical value of the Result of the Observation, if applicable and available. It is not expected that all Observations will have numeric results, rather, this field is here to house values should they exist.
This is the categorical value of the Result of the Observation, if applicable and available.

It is possible that some records destined for the Observation table have two clinical ideas represented in one source code. This is common with ICD10 codes that describe a family history of some Condition, for example. In OMOP the Vocabulary breaks these two clinical ideas into two codes; one becomes the OBSERVATION_CONCEPT_ID and the other becomes the VALUE_AS_CONCEPT_ID. It is important when using the Observation table to keep this possibility in mind and to examine the VALUE_AS_CONCEPT_ID field for relevant information.
This field contains all attributes specifying the clinical fact further, such as as degrees, severities, drug-drug interaction alerts etc.

There is currently no recommended unit for individual observation concepts. UNIT_SOURCE_VALUES should be mapped to a Standard Concept in the Unit domain that best represents the unit as given in the source data.
The provider associated with the observation record, e.g. the provider who ordered the test or the provider who recorded the result.
The visit during which the Observation occurred.

The VISIT_DETAIL record during which the Observation occurred. For example, if the Person was in the ICU at the time the VISIT_OCCURRENCE record would reflect the overall hospital stay and the VISIT_DETAIL record would reflect the ICU stay during the hospital visit.
This field houses the verbatim value from the source data representing the Observation that occurred. For example, this could be an ICD10 or Read code.

This is the concept representing the OBSERVATION_SOURCE_VALUE and may not necessarily be standard. This field is discouraged from use in analysis because it is not required to contain Standard Concepts that are used across the OHDSI community, and should only be used when Standard Concepts do not adequately represent the source detail for the Observation necessary for a given analytic use case. Consider using OBSERVATION_CONCEPT_ID instead to enable standardized analytics that can be consistent across the network.
This field houses the verbatim value from the source data representing the unit of the Observation that occurred.
This field houses the verbatim value from the source data representing the qualifier of the Observation that occurred.

This field houses the verbatim result value of the Observation from the source data.  Do not get confused with the Observation_source_value which captures source value of the observation mapped to observation_concept_id. This field is the observation result value from the source.
If the Observation record is related to another record in the database, this field is the primary key of the linked record.
If the Observation record is related to another record in the database, this field is the CONCEPT_ID that identifies which table the primary key of the linked record came from.

tables.name: observation_period
tables.description: This table contains records which define spans of time during which two conditions are expected to hold: (i) Clinical Events that happened to the Person are recorded in the Event tables, and (ii) absence of records indicate such Events did not occur during this span of time.
columns: A Person can have multiple discrete Observation Periods which are identified by the Observation_Period_Id.
The Person ID of the PERSON record for which the Observation Period is recorded.
Use this date to determine the start date of the Observation Period.
Use this date to determine the end date of the period for which we can assume that all events for a Person are recorded.
This field can be used to determine the provenance of the Observation Period as in whether the period was determined from an insurance enrollment file, EHR healthcare encounters, or other sources.

tables.name: payer_plan_period
tables.description: The PAYER_PLAN_PERIOD table captures details of the period of time that a Person is continuously enrolled under a specific health Plan benefit structure from a given Payer. Each Person receiving healthcare is typically covered by a health benefit plan, which pays for (fully or partially), or directly provides, the care. These benefit plans are provided by payers, such as health insurances or state or government agencies. In each plan the details of the health benefits are defined for the Person or her family, and the health benefit Plan might change over time typically with increasing utilization (reaching certain cost thresholds such as deductibles), plan availability and purchasing choices of the Person. The unique combinations of Payer organizations, health benefit Plans and time periods in which they are valid for a Person are recorded in this table.
columns: A unique identifier for each unique combination of a Person, Payer, Plan, and Period of time.
The Person covered by the Plan.
This field represents the organization who reimburses the provider which administers care to the Person.
This is the Payer as it appears in the source data.
This field represents the specific health benefit Plan the Person is enrolled in.
This is the health benefit Plan of the Person as it appears in the source data.
This field represents the sponsor of the Plan who finances the Plan. This includes self-insured, small group health plan and large group health plan.
The Plan sponsor as it appears in the source data.
The common identifier for all people (often a family) that covered by the same policy.
This field represents the reason the Person left the Plan, if known.
The Plan stop reason as it appears in the source data.

tables.name: person
tables.description: This table serves as the central identity management for all Persons in the database. It contains records that uniquely identify each person or patient, and some demographic information.
columns: It is assumed that every person with a different unique identifier is in fact a different person and should be treated independently.
This field is meant to capture the biological sex at birth of the Person. This field should not be used to study gender identity issues.
This field captures race or ethnic background of the person.

This field captures Ethnicity as defined by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) of the US Government: it distinguishes only between "Hispanic" and "Not Hispanic". Races and ethnic backgrounds are not stored here.
The location refers to the physical address of the person. This field should capture the last known location of the person.
The Provider refers to the last known primary care provider (General Practitioner).
The Care Site refers to where the Provider typically provides the primary care.
Use this field to link back to persons in the source data. This is typically used for error checking of ETL logic.
This field is used to store the biological sex of the person from the source data. It is not intended for use in standard analytics but for reference only.
Due to the small number of options, this tends to be zero.
This field is used to store the race of the person from the source data. It is not intended for use in standard analytics but for reference only.
Due to the small number of options, this tends to be zero.
This field is used to store the ethnicity of the person from the source data. It is not intended for use in standard analytics but for reference only.
Due to the small number of options, this tends to be zero.

tables.name: procedure_occurrence
tables.description: This table contains records of activities or processes ordered by, or carried out by, a healthcare provider on the patient with a diagnostic or therapeutic purpose.
columns: The unique key given to a procedure record for a person. Refer to the ETL for how duplicate procedures during the same visit were handled.
The PERSON_ID of the PERSON for whom the procedure is recorded. This may be a system generated code.
The PROCEDURE_CONCEPT_ID field is recommended for primary use in analyses, and must be used for network studies. This is the standard concept mapped from the source value which represents a procedure
Use this date to determine the date the procedure started.
Use this field to house the date that the procedure ended.
Use this field to house the datetime that the procedure ended.
This field can be used to determine the provenance of the Procedure record, as in whether the procedure was from an EHR system, insurance claim, registry, or other sources.
The modifiers are intended to give additional information about the procedure but as of now the vocabulary is under review.
If the quantity value is omitted, a single procedure is assumed.
The provider associated with the procedure record, e.g. the provider who performed the Procedure.
The visit during which the procedure occurred.

The VISIT_DETAIL record during which the Procedure occurred. For example, if the Person was in the ICU at the time of the Procedure the VISIT_OCCURRENCE record would reflect the overall hospital stay and the VISIT_DETAIL record would reflect the ICU stay during the hospital visit.
This field houses the verbatim value from the source data representing the procedure that occurred. For example, this could be an CPT4 or OPCS4 code.

This is the concept representing the procedure source value and may not necessarily be standard. This field is discouraged from use in analysis because it is not required to contain Standard Concepts that are used across the OHDSI community, and should only be used when Standard Concepts do not adequately represent the source detail for the Procedure necessary for a given analytic use case. Consider using PROCEDURE_CONCEPT_ID instead to enable standardized analytics that can be consistent across the network.
This field houses the verbatim value from the source data representing the modifier code for the procedure that occurred.

tables.name: provider
tables.description: The PROVIDER table contains a list of uniquely identified healthcare providers; duplication is not allowed. These are individuals providing hands-on healthcare to patients, such as physicians, nurses, midwives, physical therapists etc.
columns: It is assumed that every provider with a different unique identifier is in fact a different person and should be treated independently.
This field contains information that describes a healthcare provider.
This is the National Provider Number issued to health care providers in the US by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS).
This is the identifier issued by the DEA, a US federal agency, that allows a provider to write prescriptions for controlled substances.

This field either represents the most common specialty that occurs in the data or the most specific concept that represents all specialties listed, should the provider have more than one. This includes physician specialties such as internal medicine, emergency medicine, etc. and allied health professionals such as nurses, midwives, and pharmacists.
This is the CARE_SITE_ID for the location that the provider primarily practices in.
This field represents the recorded gender of the provider in the source data.
Use this field to link back to providers in the source data. This is typically used for error checking of ETL logic.

This refers to the specific type of healthcare provider or field of expertise listed in the source data, encompassing physician specialties like internal medicine, emergency medicine, etc., as well as allied health professionals such as nurses, midwives, and pharmacists. It covers medical specialties like surgery, internal medicine, and radiology, while other services like prosthetics, acupuncture, and physical therapy fall under the domain of "Service."
This is often zero as many sites use proprietary codes to store physician speciality.
This is provider's gender as it appears in the source data.
This is often zero as many sites use proprietary codes to store provider gender.

tables.name: relationship
tables.description: The RELATIONSHIP table provides a reference list of all types of relationships that can be used to associate any two Concepts in the CONCEPT_RELATIONSHIP table, the respective reverse relationships, and their hierarchical characteristics. Note, that Concepts representing relationships between the clinical facts, used for filling in the FACT_RELATIONSHIP table are stored in the CONCEPT table and belong to the Relationship Domain.
columns: The type of relationship captured by the relationship record.
Defines whether a relationship defines concepts into classes or hierarchies. Values are 1 for hierarchical relationship or 0 if not.
Defines whether a hierarchical relationship contributes to the concept_ancestor table. These are subsets of the hierarchical relationships. Valid values are 1 or 0.
The identifier for the relationship used to define the reverse relationship between two concepts.
A foreign key that refers to an identifier in the [CONCEPT](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html#concept) table for the unique relationship concept.

tables.name: source_to_concept_map
tables.description: The source to concept map table is recommended for use in ETL processes to maintain local source codes which are not available as Concepts in the Standardized Vocabularies, and to establish mappings for each source code into a Standard Concept as target_concept_ids that can be used to populate the Common Data Model tables. The SOURCE_TO_CONCEPT_MAP table is no longer populated with content within the Standardized Vocabularies published to the OMOP community. **There are OHDSI tools to help you populate this table; [Usagi](https://github.com/OHDSI/Usagi) and [Perseus](https://github.com/ohdsi/Perseus). You can read more about OMOP vocabulary mapping in [The Book of OHDSI Chapter 6.3](https://ohdsi.github.io/TheBookOfOhdsi/ExtractTransformLoad.html#step-2-create-the-code-mappings).**
columns: The source code being translated into a Standard Concept.
A foreign key to the Source Concept that is being translated into a Standard Concept.
A foreign key to the VOCABULARY table defining the vocabulary of the source code that is being translated to a Standard Concept.
An optional description for the source code. This is included as a convenience to compare the description of the source code to the name of the concept.
The target Concept to which the source code is being mapped.
The Vocabulary of the target Concept.
The date when the mapping instance was first recorded.
The date when the mapping instance became invalid because it was deleted or superseded (updated) by a new relationship. Default value is 31-Dec-2099.
Reason the mapping instance was invalidated. Possible values are D (deleted), U (replaced with an update) or NULL when valid_end_date has the default value.

tables.name: specimen
tables.description: The specimen domain contains the records identifying biological samples from a person.
columns: The person from whom the specimen is collected.
The date the specimen was collected.
The amount of specimen collected from the person.
The unit for the quantity of the specimen.
This is the site on the body where the specimen is from.
This is the identifier for the specimen from the source system.

tables.name: visit_detail
tables.description: The VISIT_DETAIL table is an optional table used to represents details of each record in the parent VISIT_OCCURRENCE table. A good example of this would be the movement between units in a hospital during an inpatient stay or claim lines associated with a one insurance claim. For every record in the VISIT_OCCURRENCE table there may be 0 or more records in the VISIT_DETAIL table with a 1:n relationship where n may be 0. The VISIT_DETAIL table is structurally very similar to VISIT_OCCURRENCE table and belongs to the visit domain.
columns: Use this to identify unique interactions between a person and the health care system. This identifier links across the other CDM event tables to associate events with a visit detail.
This field contains a concept id representing the kind of visit detail, like inpatient or outpatient. All concepts in this field should be standard and belong to the Visit domain.
This is the date of the start of the encounter. This may or may not be equal to the date of the Visit the Visit Detail is associated with.

This the end date of the patient-provider interaction.  If a Person is still an inpatient in the hospital at the time of the data extract and does not have a visit_end_date, then set the visit_end_date to the date of the data pull.
If a Person is still an inpatient in the hospital at the time of the data extract and does not have a visit_end_datetime, then set the visit_end_datetime to the datetime of the data pull.
Use this field to understand the provenance of the visit detail record, or where the record comes from.

There will only be one provider per  **visit** record and the ETL document should clearly state how they were chosen (attending, admitting, etc.). This is a typical reason for leveraging the VISIT_DETAIL table as even though each VISIT_DETAIL record can only have one provider, there is no limit to the number of VISIT_DETAIL records that can be associated to a VISIT_OCCURRENCE record.
This field provides information about the Care Site where the Visit Detail took place.
This field houses the verbatim value from the source data representing the kind of visit detail that took place (inpatient, outpatient, emergency, etc.)

Use this field to determine where the patient was admitted from. This concept is part of the visit domain and can indicate if a patient was admitted to the hospital from a long-term care facility, for example.

Use this field to determine where the patient was discharged to after a visit. columns: Use this to identify unique interactions between a person and the health care system. This identifier links across the other CDM event tables to associate events with a visit.

For inpatient visits, the start date is typically the admission date. For outpatient visits the start date and end date will be the same.

For inpatient visits the end date is typically the discharge date.  If a Person is still an inpatient in the hospital at the time of the data extract and does not have a visit_end_date, then set the visit_end_date to the date of the data pull.
If a Person is still an inpatient in the hospital at the time of the data extract and does not have a visit_end_datetime, then set the visit_end_datetime to the datetime of the data pull.
